summary: Summation No. 19 covers April 1947 (with economic statistics mostly for March and February) in four parts: General digest, Political, Economic and Social. April was dominated by Japan's first postwar full cycle of elections under the new Constitution: governors and mayors on 5 April, the House of Councillors on 20 April, the House of Representatives on 25 April and prefectural assemblies on 30 April, with MacArthur praising the result on 27 April. The Social Democrats became the largest lower-house party, independents dominated executive posts, and the purge screened 190,685 persons. The economic chapters show recovery driven by better coal deliveries (March coal 2,256,600 tons), postwar-peak pig iron, steel, pulp, paper and raw silk, with tightening food collection, black-market crackdowns, price rises, a new antitrust act, zaibatsu liquidation and trade-union consolidation. Social chapters give nutrition and disease data, repatriation totals, and education, religion and press developments. A historian will find detailed election returns, Diet statistics, war-crimes trial tables and sector statistics.
highlights: Japanese voters went to the polls four times: 5 April for 46 governors and local executives, 20 April for the House of Councillors, 25 April for the House of Representatives and 30 April for prefectural and local assemblies; MacArthur's 27 April message said the Japanese people had rejected communism.

In the House of Representatives election the Social Democrats won 143 of 466 seats, ahead of Liberals 132, Democrats 126, People's Cooperatives 31, Communists 4 and minor parties 18; in the Councillors election independents took 110 of 250 seats and Social Democrats led the parties with 47.

Independents won 29 governorships and 3,716 village headships on 5 April; Seiichiro Yasui beat Social Democrat Daikichiro Tagawa 705,040 to 615,622 in Tokyo, and Toshibuni Tanaka became the Socialist governor of Hokkaido after a run-off.

The purge screened 5,327 election candidates (190 barred) and 190,685 persons from 29 March to 26 April; Welfare Minister Yoshinari Kawai and several Democratic Party leaders were purged, and the Public Office Qualifications Appeals Board began work.

The Diet passed the antitrust Act Relating to Prohibition of Private Monopoly on 31 March, creating a seven-member Fair Trade Commission; the Holding Company Liquidation Commission took title to shares of 65 holding companies worth 5,154,152,000 yen.

March coal output was 2,256,600 metric tons, 230,500 under quota; improved deliveries lifted pig iron and steel ingots to a postwar peak, paper to 34,168 short tons and electric power to 2,432,541,000 kWh, a 21 percent gain over February.

Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 122,400,000,000 yen on 30 April, the increased income tax yield estimate rose from 4.5 to 16 billion yen, and electric power rates were raised 300 percent on 1 April.

Coal-miners' industry-wide contract signed 12 April covering 203,316 underground workers; union membership stood at 5,326,969 in 19,983 unions on 31 March, and over half of organized labor was now under recent agreements.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 19, April 1947, the four-part table of contents, and the list of 108 charts, maps and graphs with page numbers.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no SCAP reorganization, the four elections, purge and war crimes figures, economic gains in coal, steel and textiles, and health, education and press items.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: One-line report that there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during April 1947.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Summary of the four elections choosing 232,863 officials, with Social Democrats winning 143 lower-house seats, 190 candidates purged, and 46 war-crimes arrest orders.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of land purchases of 151,566 cho, record pig iron and steel output, textile gains, Bank of Japan notes at 122.4 billion yen and 4,153,369 tons of rice collected.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of the February nutrition survey, 62,327 repatriates, the Education Ministry's teacher conferences, shrine land notification, 18,000,000 Constitution pamphlets and press comment.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed reports on the April elections, the 92nd Diet, the purge, public safety and crime statistics, and war-crimes investigations, trials and the Tokyo Tribunal defense case.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Election results for governors, Councillors, Representatives and assemblies, the 92nd Diet record, the purge of 190,685 persons screened, and labor-union endorsements and successes.

sections.title: The General Elections
sections.summary: MacArthur's 27 April statement, tallies of executive, Councillors, Representatives and prefectural-assembly elections, with fraud cases and run-offs in eight prefectures.

sections.title: Executive Elections (5 April)
sections.summary: Election of 46 governors, 309 mayors and village heads, independents winning 29 governorships, 70.8 percent turnout, Yasui's 705,040 to 615,622 win in Tokyo and the run-offs.

sections.title: House of Councillors Election (20 April)
sections.summary: Candidate lists, about 32,000,000 voters, results of 110 independents and 47 Social Democrats among 250 seats, occupational analysis, press comment and the list of those elected.

sections.title: House of Representatives Election (25 April)
sections.summary: Party predictions, 1,573 candidates for 466 seats, and results giving Social Democrats 143 seats, Liberals 132 and Democrats 126, with press reaction.

sections.title: Prefectural and Local Assembly Elections (30 April)
sections.summary: 7,130 candidates for 2,502 prefectural seats; independents won 771 seats and controlled 13 assemblies, Democrats 517, Liberals 468, Social Democrats 414.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Statistics for the 95-day 92nd Diet: 173 measures submitted, 18,743 visitors, 315 petitions, eight demonstrations and changing party strength as the Democratic Party formed.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: 190,685 persons screened 29 March-26 April, 5,327 candidates examined with 190 barred, prominent Democrats purged, about 1,160 local executives barred and an appeals board begun.

sections.title: Labor and Politics
sections.summary: Union endorsements by NCIU (1,643,599 members) and the General Federation, and labor leaders winning 32 of 350 Councillor seats and 16 Representatives seats.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Elections held without serious incident but 490 election-law cases; new black-market penalties up to 100,000 yen, 634 rail deaths in the first quarter, February crime of 129,440 offenses and prison statistics.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: War-crimes investigations (1,749 cases on hand), 46 persons ordered apprehended, trial results in Japan and the Philippines, and the defense case at the Tokyo Tribunal.

sections.title: Legal Affairs, Investigation, Apprehension and Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Case counts of 1,558 rising to 1,749, 80 persons delivered to Sugamo, eleven Japan trials with 23 defendants, and Philippine trials yielding five death sentences.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals (Tokyo Tribunal)
sections.summary: Proceedings against Okawa discontinued on 9 April, the Manchurian phase of the defense ended 21 April and the China phase began 22 April, with witness testimony summaries.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Twelve sections of production, trade, price, finance and property statistics, mostly for March 1947, showing coal-led recovery, tight food supply, price increases and economic deconcentration.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Local Land Commissions bought 151,566 cho in March, prefectural retention rates were set, March fish landings totaled 101,815 tons, and the kiji was named national bird.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: March log output 734,928,000 board feet, coal 2,256,600 tons with a 27,000,000-ton 1947-48 goal, lignite 231,197 tons, the 12 April miners' contract and oil drilling results.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 136,800 tons, postwar-peak pig iron and steel at 60 percent of the minimum need, aluminum 1,869 tons, copper, rubber, cement, fertilizer, chemicals and machinery output.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Food-processing shortages, pulp up 36 percent and paper 34,168 short tons, glass, medical supplies, electrical goods, truck chassis, leather, handicrafts and sewing machines.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Raw silk reached a postwar peak, with cotton, rayon, wool and knit-goods output rising on eased power limits and better coal and raw-material deliveries.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Government railways carried 270,899,116 passengers and 9,433,500 tons of freight in March; electric power generated 2,432,541,000 kWh, up 21 percent; gas industry data.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: New Labor Bureau at the Communications Ministry, 44 radio stations licensed, coastal radio opened to Allied ships, radiotelegraph to the United States on 18 April, and 5,700,000 licensed receivers.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Employment exchange reorganization of 8 April, 19,983 unions with 5,326,969 members, the coal miners' 12 April agreement, Central Labor Relations Committee elections and employment programs.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Little change in March trade, with sample shipments including 40 cases of crabmeat to the United States and textile, machinery, chemical and wood-product samples to Europe and Asia.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Government food stocks of 38 days, 4,153,369 tons of rice collected, 112,026 tons of imports released, electric rates up 300 percent, and new salt, lime, coke and petroleum prices.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 122.4 billion yen, licenses to Times Publishing, Northwest and Pan American, income-tax estimate raised to 16 billion yen, and April borrowing of 12,910,624,720 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control
sections.summary: Allied and looted property tallies, dissolved organizations' accounts, the 31 March antitrust act with a Fair Trade Commission, and liquidation of 65 holding companies' shares worth 5.15 billion yen.

sections.title: Antitrust and Cartels
sections.summary: 26 restricted concerns allowed 82,675,838 yen for rehabilitation, the new antitrust act's prohibitions and the seven-member Fair Trade Commission, and Zaibatsu family designations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, nutrition and repatriation figures, followed by education, religion, arts, information programs, press and cultural activity during April 1947.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: February nutrition surveys showing improvement, a Tokyo typhus outbreak of 35 cases, 3,172 hospitals, patent medicine output of 117,497,793 yen and 62,327 Japanese repatriated.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher-training conferences, shrine and temple land notification of 2 April, election broadcasting, 18,000,000 Constitution pamphlets, press comment and 17,142 visitors to the SCAP library.
